summary: Someone who sold his family field must wait at least two years of crops before he buys it back.

chunks.en: Someone who sells his field at a time when Yovel is kept
chunks.st: One who sells his field during a period when the Jubilee Year is in effect

chunks.he: אֵינוֹ מֻתָּר לִגְאוֹל פָּחוּת מִשְּׁתֵּי שָׁנִים,
chunks.en: may not buy it back before two years,
chunks.st: is not permitted to redeem it less than two years after the sale,

chunks.en: as it says (Vayikra 25),
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.en: "By the number of years of crops he shall sell to you."
chunks.st: “According to the number of years of the crops he shall sell to you” (Leviticus 25:15).
chunks.stMore: The plural form “years” indicates a minimum of two years.

chunks.he: הָיְתָה שְׁנַת שִׁדָּפוֹן וְיֵרָקוֹן אוֹ שְׁבִיעִית,
chunks.en: If there was a year of blight or mildew, or Shemittah,
chunks.explain: These are years when the field gives no crops for the buyer.
chunks.st: If one of those years was a year of blight or mildew, or if it was the Sabbatical Year,
chunks.stMore: when the buyer is unable to derive benefit from the field,

chunks.en: it does not count.
chunks.st: that year does not count as part of the tally,
chunks.stMore: and the owner must wait an additional year before redeeming the field.

chunks.en: If the buyer plowed it, or left it empty,
chunks.st: If the buyer plowed the field but did not sow it, or if he left it fallow,

chunks.en: it counts for him.
chunks.st: that year counts as part of his tally,
chunks.stMore: as it was fit to produce a crop.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: if he sold it to him before Rosh
chunks.st: If the owner of the field sold it to the buyer before Rosh

chunks.en: Hashanah, when it was full of fruit,
chunks.st: HaShana and the field was full of produce,
chunks.stMore: and the owner redeems the field after two years,

chunks.en: the buyer eats from it
chunks.st: that buyer consumes from

chunks.en: three crops in two years.
chunks.st: the field’s produce three crops in two years.
chunks.stMore: Although he received the field with its crop, he is not required to return it in the same state.

summary: When the owner buys back his field, which price does he count by? And some ways of buying back that are allowed with hekdesh but not with a regular person.
stIntro: When the Jubilee Year is in effect, one may sell a field only until the Jubilee Year, at which point the field returns to its original owner. If the owner redeems the field before the Jubilee Year, the payment per annum is calculated by dividing the sale price by the number of years from the sale until the Jubilee Year. The owner returns the per annum payment multiplied by the number of years remaining until the Jubilee Year.

chunks.en: If he sold it to the first buyer for a maneh,
chunks.st: If the owner of a field sold it to the first buyer for one hundred dinars

chunks.en: and the first sold it to the second for two hundred,
chunks.st: and the first buyer then sold it to the second buyer for two hundred dinars,

chunks.en: he counts only by the first price,
chunks.st: when the original owner redeems the field he calculates the payment only according to the price that he set with the first buyer,

chunks.en: as it says, "to the man to whom he sold it."
chunks.st: as it is stated: “And he calculates the years of its sale, and he returns the remainder to the man to whom he sold it” (Leviticus 25:27).

chunks.en: If he sold it to the first buyer for two hundred,
chunks.st: If the owner of a field sold it to the first buyer for two hundred dinars

chunks.en: and the first sold it to the second for a maneh,
chunks.st: and the first buyer then sold it to the second buyer for one hundred dinars,

chunks.en: he counts only by the last price,
chunks.st: when the original owner redeems the field, he calculates the payment only according to the price that was paid by the last buyer,

chunks.en: as it says (there),
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.en: "to the man": to the man who has the field now.
chunks.st: “And he calculates the years of its sale, and he returns the remainder to the man to whom he sold it.” The superfluous term “to the man” indicates that the verse is referring to the man who is currently in possession of the field.

chunks.en: He may not sell a field far away to buy back a field nearby,
chunks.st: One may not sell his ancestral field that is located in a distant area and redeem with the proceeds a field that he sold in a nearby area.

chunks.en: or sell a poor field to buy back a good one.
chunks.st: Likewise, he may not sell a low-quality field and redeem with the proceeds a high-quality field.

chunks.en: He may not borrow money to buy it back,
chunks.st: And he may not borrow money and redeem the field,

chunks.en: and he may not buy it back in halves.
chunks.st: nor may he redeem the field incrementally, half now and half at a later date.

chunks.en: But with hekdesh, all of these are allowed.
chunks.st: But with regard to redeeming a field from the Temple treasury, it is permitted to redeem the field in any of these ways.

chunks.en: Here, a regular person's field is stricter than hekdesh.
chunks.st: This is a halakha where greater stringency applies with regard to redeeming a field from an ordinary individual than with regard to redeeming it from the Temple treasury.

summary: A house in a walled city can be bought back only within one year of the sale. How the year is counted.

chunks.en: Someone who sells a house in a city with a wall,
chunks.st: One who sells a house from among the houses of walled cities

chunks.en: may buy it back right away,
chunks.st: may redeem the house immediately, even without the consent of the buyer,

chunks.en: and he may buy it back the whole twelve months.
chunks.st: and he may redeem the house during the entire twelve months following the sale,

chunks.he: הֲרֵי זֶה כְּמִין רִבִּית וְאֵינָהּ רִבִּית.
chunks.en: This looks like a kind of ribbis, but it is not ribbis.
chunks.explain: Ribbis is extra money paid for a loan, which is forbidden.
chunks.st: When he redeems the house within the twelve-month period, he returns the sale price to the buyer, and this is ostensibly like a form of interest, as the buyer has effectively resided in the house for free in exchange for the fact that the buyer’s money was in the possession of the seller. It is not considered interest,
chunks.stMore: because the buyer owned the house during the period in which he resided in it.

chunks.en: If the seller died,
chunks.st: If the seller died,

chunks.en: his son may buy it back.
chunks.st: his son may redeem the house from the buyer.

chunks.en: If the buyer died,
chunks.st: If the buyer died,

chunks.en: he may buy it back from the buyer's son.
chunks.st: the seller may redeem it from the possession of the buyer’s son.

chunks.en: The year is counted for him only
chunks.st: If the buyer sold the house to another, one calculates the year

chunks.en: from the time he sold it to him,
chunks.st: only from the time that the owner sold the house to the first buyer,

chunks.en: as it says (there),
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.en: "until a full year is over for him."
chunks.st: “And if it is not redeemed until the passage of a full year for him,
chunks.stMore: then the house that is in the walled city shall stand in possession of the one who bought it in perpetuity” (Leviticus 25:30). The term “for him” indicates that the year is calculated from when the initial owner sold the house.

chunks.en: And when it says "full,"
chunks.st: When it says: “A full year,” this serves

chunks.en: it includes the extra month of a leap year.
chunks.st: to include the intercalated month in the year calculated from the sale, if it was a leap year.

chunks.en: Rebbi says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi says:

chunks.en: he gives him a year and its extra days.
chunks.explain: A sun year, which is longer than a moon year.
chunks.st: The word “full” serves to give the seller a year and its addition, i.e., the year during which the house may be redeemed is not the 354-day lunar year, but the 365-day solar year.

summary: If a house in a walled city is not bought back within the year, it belongs to the buyer forever. Hillel made a takanah so a buyer could not hide to stop the seller from paying.

chunks.en: If the last day of the twelve
chunks.st: If the final day of the twelve-month period

chunks.en: months came and it was not bought back,
chunks.st: arrived and the house was not redeemed,

chunks.en: it belongs to him forever,
chunks.st: the house has become the property of the buyer in perpetuity.

chunks.he: אֶחָד הַלּוֹקֵחַ וְאֶחָד שֶׁנִּתַּן לוֹ מַתָּנָה,
chunks.en: whether he bought it or it was given to him as a present,
chunks.st: This is the halakha with regard to both one who buys a house in a walled city and one to whom it is given as a gift,

chunks.en: as it says, "forever."
chunks.st: as it is stated: “Then the house that is in the walled city shall stand in possession of the one who bought it in perpetuity” (Leviticus 25:30).

chunks.en: At first, the buyer would hide on the last day
chunks.st: At first, the buyer would conceal himself on the final

chunks.en: of the twelve months,
chunks.st: day of the twelve-month period,

chunks.en: so that it would be his forever.
chunks.st: in order to ensure that it would become his in perpetuity.

chunks.en: Hillel Hazaken made a takanah,
chunks.st: Hillel instituted that

words.note: Hillel was a great leader, before the Tannaim of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: that the seller would leave his money in the special room,
chunks.st: the seller would place [ḥolesh] his money in the chamber of the court

chunks.en: and break the door and go in.
chunks.st: and that he will break the door and enter the house,

chunks.en: Whenever the other man wants,
chunks.st: and when the other individual, i.e., the buyer, will wish to do so,

chunks.en: he can come and take his money.
chunks.st: he may come to the chamber and take his money.

summary: Which places inside a walled city count like houses of a walled city? The Tannaim argue about fields and about a house built into the wall.

chunks.en: Everything that is inside the wall
chunks.st: The halakhic status of any area that is located within the city wall

chunks.en: is like the houses of walled cities,
chunks.st: is like that of the houses of walled cities

chunks.en: except for the fields.
chunks.st: except for the fields located therein.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: even the fields.
chunks.st: Even the fields are included in this category.

chunks.en: A house built into the wall:
chunks.st: With regard to a house that is built in the wall itself,

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: it is not like the houses of walled cities.
chunks.st: Its halakhic status is not like that of the houses of walled cities.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: its outside wall counts as its city wall.
chunks.st: The outer wall of the house is considered the city wall, and therefore it has the status of a house in a walled city.

summary: Which cities count as walled cities: they must have had a wall since the days of Yehoshua bin Nun.

chunks.en: A city whose roofs are its wall,
chunks.st: The halakhic status of a house in a city whose houses are attached and their rooftops constitute the top of its wall,

chunks.en: or that was not surrounded by a wall since the days of
chunks.st: and likewise, the status of a house in a city that is not surrounded by a wall from the era of

chunks.en: Yehoshua bin Nun,
chunks.st: Joshua, son of Nun,
chunks.stMore: even if a surrounding wall was constructed during a later period,

chunks.en: is not like the houses of walled cities.
chunks.st: is not like that of the houses of walled cities.

chunks.en: And these are the houses of walled cities:
chunks.st: And these are the houses of walled cities:

chunks.he: שָׁלשׁ חֲצֵרוֹת שֶׁל שְׁנֵי שְׁנֵי בָתִּים,
chunks.en: a city of three courtyards with two houses each,
chunks.st: Any city in which there are at least three courtyards, each containing two houses,

chunks.he: מֻקָּפוֹת חוֹמָה מִימוֹת יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן,
chunks.en: with a wall around it since the days of Yehoshua bin Nun,
chunks.st: and which is surrounded by a wall from the era of Joshua, son of Nun,

chunks.en: like the old fort of Tzippori,
chunks.st: e.g., the ancient fort [katzra] of Tzippori,

chunks.en: the fortress of Gush Chalav,
chunks.st: and the fortress [ḥakra] of Gush Ḥalav,

chunks.en: old Yodfat,
chunks.st: and ancient Yodfat,

chunks.en: Gamla, Gedod,
chunks.st: and Gamla, and Gedod,

chunks.en: Chadid, Ono,
chunks.st: and Ḥadid, and Ono,

chunks.en: and Yerushalayim, and other cities like them.
chunks.st: and Jerusalem, and likewise other similar cities.

summary: Houses in towns without walls get the good rules of walled-city houses and the good rules of fields.

chunks.en: Houses in towns without walls,
chunks.st: With regard to the houses of the unwalled courtyards mentioned in the Torah (see Leviticus 25:31),
chunks.stMore: i.e., houses in villages that are not surrounded by walls,

chunks.en: get the good rules of the houses of
chunks.st: one accords them the exceptional provisions that apply to houses of

words.en: that is in the houses of

chunks.en: walled cities and the good rules of fields.
chunks.st: walled cities and the exceptional provisions that apply to fields.

chunks.en: They can be bought back right away,
chunks.st: Therefore, they are redeemed immediately

chunks.he: וְנִגְאָלִין כָּל שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ כַּבָּתִּים,
chunks.en: and during the whole twelve months, like houses.
chunks.st: and for the entire twelve months following the sale, like in the sale of houses of walled cities,
chunks.stMore: and not like fields, which may be redeemed only after two years.

chunks.en: And they go back at Yovel, and the price goes down each year, like fields.
chunks.st: And they leave the possession of the buyer during the Jubilee Year or with a per annum deduction from the money of the sale price, like the sale of fields.
chunks.stMore: By contrast, houses of walled cities become the possession of the buyer in perpetuity after one year, and if they are redeemed within the year, one pays the full sale price.

chunks.en: And these are the houses in towns without walls:
chunks.st: And these are the houses of the unwalled courtyards
chunks.stMore: whose halakha was taught in the previous mishna:

chunks.he: שְׁתֵּי חֲצֵרוֹת שֶׁל שְׁנֵי שְׁנֵי בָתִּים,
chunks.en: a town of two courtyards with two houses each,
chunks.st: Any city in which there are two courtyards each containing two houses,

chunks.en: even if it is surrounded by a wall
chunks.st: although it is surrounded by a wall

chunks.en: since the days of Yehoshua bin Nun,
chunks.st: from the era of Joshua, son of Nun,

chunks.en: these are like houses in towns without walls.
chunks.st: their halakhic status is like that of the houses of the unwalled courtyards.

summary: The special rules for the houses of Levi'im, and what may be changed in the land around the cities of the Levi'im and of other Jews.

chunks.en: A Yisrael who inherited from his mother's father, a Levi,
chunks.st: An Israelite who inherited a house in a walled city from his mother’s father who was a Levite

chunks.en: does not buy back in this order.
chunks.explain: He may buy it back at any time, like a Levi.
chunks.st: does not redeem the house in accordance with this procedure delineated in the previous mishnayot;
chunks.stMore: rather, if he sold the inherited house, he may redeem it always, like a Levite.

chunks.en: And also a Levi who inherited from
chunks.st: And likewise, a Levite who inherited

chunks.en: his mother's father, a Yisrael,
chunks.st: a house in a walled city from his mother’s father who was an Israelite

chunks.en: does not buy back in this order,
chunks.st: does not redeem the house in accordance with this procedure delineated in the previous mishnayot.

chunks.en: as it says (Vayikra 25),
chunks.st: The mishna provides the source for these halakhot: As it is stated:
chunks.stMore: “And if a man purchases from the Levites, the house that was sold in the city of his possession shall go out during the Jubilee Year;

chunks.en: "For the houses of the cities of the Levi'im":
chunks.st: as the houses of the cities of the Levites are their possession

chunks.en: only when he is a Levi and in the cities of the Levi'im,
chunks.st: The verse indicates that the ability to always redeem the house of a Levite does not apply unless the one selling the house will be a Levite and the house is located in the cities of the Levites.

chunks.en: says Rebbi.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi.

chunks.en: And the Chachamim say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.he: אֵין הַדְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים אֶלָּא בְעָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם.
chunks.en: these words are said only about the cities of the Levi'im.
chunks.st: These matters are stated only with regard to a house in the cities of the Levites, even if the owner was not a Levite.
chunks.stMore: The Levites received two thousand cubits surrounding their cities, one thousand cubits of empty lots and one thousand cubits for fields and vineyards.

chunks.en: We may not make a field into an open lot,
chunks.st: One may neither render a field an empty lot

words.note: Open land around a city, with no fields or houses.

chunks.en: or an open lot into a field,
chunks.st: nor an empty lot a field.

chunks.he: וְלֹא מִגְרָשׁ עִיר וְלֹא עִיר מִגְרָשׁ.
chunks.en: or an open lot into city, or city into an open lot.
chunks.st: Similarly, one may neither incorporate an empty lot into a city nor render part of a city an empty lot.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar said:

chunks.en: when is this said?
chunks.st: In what case is this statement said?

chunks.en: In the cities of the Levi'im.
chunks.st: It applies in the cities of the Levites.

chunks.en: But in the cities of Yisrael,
chunks.st: But in the cities of the Israelites

chunks.he: עוֹשִׂין שָׂדֶה מִגְרָשׁ וְלֹא מִגְרָשׁ שָׂדֶה,
chunks.en: we may make a field into an open lot, but not an open lot into a field,
chunks.st: one may render a field an empty lot but not an empty lot a field,

chunks.en: an open lot into city, but not city into an open lot,
chunks.st: and one may incorporate an empty lot into a city but not render part of a city an empty lot,

chunks.he: כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יַחֲרִיבוּ אֶת עָרֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.
chunks.en: so that they do not ruin the cities of Yisrael.
chunks.st: in order to ensure that they will not thereby destroy the cities of Israel.

chunks.he: הַכֹּהֲנִים וְהַלְוִיִּם מוֹכְרִים לְעוֹלָם וְגוֹאֲלִים לְעוֹלָם,
chunks.en: The Kohanim and the Levi'im may sell at any time and buy back at any time,
chunks.st: The priests and the Levites may sell their fields and houses always and may redeem them always,

chunks.en: as it says (there),
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.en: "The Levi'im shall always be able to buy back."
chunks.st: “The Levites shall have a perpetual right of redemption” (Leviticus 25:32). Priests are also members of the tribe of Levi.
